note: Small primitive campground on the west bank of the Gasconade River at the end of County Road 201 (about 8 miles of county road from US 63): a gravel loop with a privy, four short gravel back-in pads off the loop into a mown, lightly shaded island, and two more spots on the grass between the loop and the riverbank, 15-25 m from the water through a single line of bank trees. The boat ramp is at the south end of the loop. The pads look 12-15 m long on imagery; spot length is not published. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: MDC 'Individual Campsites' - six mapped Primitive Camping symbols and six GIS points around a gravel loop with pads and a privy, separate from the ramp. Free, FCFS, no hookups, 14-day limit. Two of the six spots are on the riverbank: waterfront lead (stored not waterfront). Pin fine. Phone matches.
flags: INCLUSION (lot rule - stays): the area page lists 'Camping: Individual Campsites', says 'access to the Gasconade River with a boat ramp and primitive camping allowed' and captions a photo 'Campground at Paydown Access by the Gasconade River'. The map (06/12) draws six Primitive Camping Area symbols around the loop road, four on its west leg and inside the loop and two on the river side of its east leg; GIS layer 27 has six 'Primitive Camping Area' points (OBJECTIDs 72, 73, 74, 544, 545, 546). On the 0.22 m/px leaf-off frame the loop is ~110 x 60 m of gravel road with three gravel back-in spurs off the west leg and one off the east leg (each about 12-15 m), a gravel parking pad and a privy inside the loop, and the concrete ramp at the south end ~90 m from the nearest pad. This is a small designated campground, not a ramp lot. A 23-ft rig fits the pads as seen.

ACCESS: MDC's directions are 'Highway 63 north 5.50 miles, then County Road 201 east (right) 8 miles to the access'; the map labels it a gravel road. The page says nothing of a ford, low-water crossing or 4WD. I could not check the 8 miles for a creek crossing: the Overpass mirror did not answer (OSM unread) and I did not trace the road on imagery.

WATERFRONT LEAD (stored not waterfront) - UPGRADE CANDIDATE, owner's call: the Gasconade is ~120 m wide here. GIS points 544 (38.23100,-91.81420) and 545 (38.23073,-91.81417) and the map's two east-side symbols sit on the strip between the loop's east leg and the bank, 15-25 m from the water's edge, with only a single line of leafless bank trees between - no road, lot or day use between spot and water (the loop road is behind them). The other four spots are inside or west of the loop, 50-75 m from the water with the loop road and the bank-side spots between: a view at best. Read against the rules: two of six spots look riverfront (or riverview if the bank trees are judged a screen in leaf); the campground as a whole would be riverview by the loop-road rule. I could not confirm a view in leaf - the only frame is leaf-off, and the page's one photo was not opened. The stored waterfront_evidence was not in the dossier.
